question.problem:
Evaluate ${f}_{yzx}(2,1,3)$ given that a function $f(x,y,z)$ and all of its higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ and that

$$
{f}_{xy}(x,y,z)=\sqrt{x-y+z}-\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y+z)
$$
question.worked_solution:
As the higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yzx}(x,y,z) & ={f}_{xyz}(x,y,z) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({f}_{xz}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\sqrt{x-y+z}-\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y+z)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x-y+z}}-\frac{1}{x+y+z}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point  $(2,1,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yzx}(2,1,3) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2-1+3}}-\frac{1}{2+1+3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}}-\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\end{aligned}
$$
